text: 57-year-old male. The patient reports a large wound on his right lower leg that has been present for 6 months. speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history. Given your family history of leg swelling and previous DVT, do you experience significant pain, heaviness, or visible varicose veins in that leg? REQUEST TEST: D-Dimer; REQUEST TEST: Venous_Doppler_Ultrasound.

text: RESULTS: D-Dimer: Not measured per current data; Venous_Doppler_Ultrasound: Evidence of venous reflux and obstruction in superficial and deep venous systems of the right leg

speaker: Patient

speaker: Doctor
text: The family history and your previous DVT strongly suggest venous insufficiency as the cause of your chronic wound. speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Deep vein thrombosis in the right leg 5 years prior. No other significant medical history. Social history: Non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially. Works as an accountant.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Venous Insufficiency with Venous Stasis Ulcer. The history of DVT, chronic unilateral leg swelling, family history, and a chronic wound on the right lower leg are classic for this condition.
